summary: This article explains how wind turbines turn moving air into electricity, why wind farms are a clean source of power with some challenges, and how Saudi Arabia has begun using wind energy at Dumat Al Jandal.
introduce: Write “Problem” and “Solution” on the board and give pairs thirty seconds to think of a problem people face in daily life and one way to fix it. Explain that as they read “Wind Farms: Power from the Air”, they will look for the main problem and how it is solved.

keyTerms.def: a machine that changes motion into electricity
able to be used again and again because nature keeps replacing it
a form of energy that flows through wires and powers lights and machines

challengeTerms.def: having to do with motion; kinetic energy is the energy something has because it is moving
located in the sea, away from the coast
stopping and starting again; not steady

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that every country should build more wind farms? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain the advantages and one problem of wind power.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review generator, renewable, and electricity, and let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use kinetic, offshore, and intermittent in a short paragraph that suggests a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
